description: ResearchLens V1.0 Baseline Evaluation Benchmark Dataset
reference_corpus: Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani et al., 2017)

questions.question: What is the primary architectural contribution of the Transformer model compared to earlier sequence transduction models?
questions.reference_answer: The Transformer is the first sequence transduction model based entirely on self-attention mechanisms to compute representations of its input and output, completely dispensing with recurrence and convolutions like RNNs and CNNs.

questions.question: How is Scaled Dot-Product Attention mathematically defined, and why is the scaling factor sqrt(d_k) introduced?
questions.reference_answer: Scaled Dot-Product Attention is computed as Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k))V. The scaling factor 1/sqrt(d_k) is introduced because for large values of d_k, the dot products grow large in magnitude, pushing the softmax function into regions with extremely small gradients.

questions.question: How does Multi-Head Attention work and what benefit does it provide over single attention?
questions.reference_answer: Multi-Head Attention linearly projects queries, keys, and values h times with different, learned linear projections to d_k, d_k, and d_v dimensions, computes attention in parallel on each, and concatenates the results. It allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions.

questions.question: How does the Transformer inject positional information since it contains no recurrence or convolution?
questions.reference_answer: The Transformer uses Positional Encodings added to the input embeddings at the bottoms of the encoder and decoder stacks. It uses sine and cosine functions of different frequencies: PE(pos, 2i) = sin(pos / 10000^(2i/d_model)) and PE(pos, 2i+1) = cos(pos / 10000^(2i/d_model)).

questions.question: What BLEU scores did the Transformer achieve on the WMT 2014 English-to-German and English-to-French translation benchmarks?
questions.reference_answer: On the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, the Transformer (big) achieved a BLEU score of 28.4, outperforming previous best models by over 2.0 BLEU. On the English-to-French task, it established a state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8.

questions.question: Compare the computational complexity per layer of Self-Attention against Recurrent and Convolutional layers.
questions.reference_answer: Self-attention has a per-layer complexity of O(n^2 * d) where n is sequence length and d is representation dimension, with O(1) sequential operations. Recurrent layers have O(n * d^2) complexity with O(n) sequential operations. Convolutional layers have O(k * n * d^2) complexity with O(1) sequential operations.

questions.question: What optimizer and learning rate schedule were used to train the baseline Transformer?
questions.reference_answer: The models were trained using the Adam optimizer with beta_1 = 0.9, beta_2 = 0.98, and epsilon = 10^-9. The learning rate was varied according to a formula that increases linearly for warmup_steps (4000) and decreases proportionally to the inverse square root of the step number.

questions.question: What regularization methods were applied during the training of the Transformer?
questions.reference_answer: The authors applied Residual Dropout (rate P_drop = 0.1) to the output of each sub-layer before addition and normalization, as well as to sums of embeddings and positional encodings. They also used Label Smoothing with epsilon_ls = 0.1.

questions.question: Why is masking applied to the self-attention sub-layer in the decoder?
questions.reference_answer: Masking combined with shifting output embeddings by one position ensures that predictions for position i can depend only on known outputs at positions less than i, preserving the auto-regressive property and preventing the decoder from attending to subsequent future positions.

questions.question: What were the hyperparameter differences between the Transformer base model and the Transformer big model?
questions.reference_answer: The base model used N=6 layers, d_model=512, d_ff=2048, h=8 heads, d_k=d_v=64, with 65M parameters. The big model increased d_model to 1024, d_ff to 4096, h to 16 heads, d_k=d_v=64, with 213M parameters and 0.3 dropout.
